channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: O isolamento de Flávio Bolsonaro na nova podridão do sistema político
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's partisan isolation reflects a shift in Brazilian politics where Congress has gained power at the expense of the Executive, diminishing the importance of personal alliances with the president for controlling state resources. This trend extends beyond elections and signals a structural reorganization of the political system, characterized by greater fragmentation and reliance on parliamentary negotiations.

item.title: Michelle nega apoio a Ciro Gomes no Ceará
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro reiterated that she will not support Ciro Gomes in Ceará, even after Eduardo Girão withdrew from the state race. Girão, her former preferred candidate, is now running as vice president on Romeu Zema’s ticket. She maintains her opposition to the former Ceará governor.

item.title: Com Neymar no banco, Santos está escalado para jogo contra o Remo
item.description: Santos faces Remo at Mangueirão in Belém in the second leg of the Copa do Brasil round of 16, following a 0-0 draw in the first leg. Coach Cuca has named Neymar on the bench, making four changes to the starting XI: Gabriel Menino, Adonis Frías, João Schmidt and Caballero replace Igor Vinícius, Lucas Veríssimo, Rollheiser and Neymar. Remo’s lineup remains unchanged.

item.title: Brasil acusa EUA de escalada hostil após revogar visto de embaixadora
item.description: The Brazilian government accused the United States of deliberately escalating hostile measures by revoking the visa of Ambassador Maria Luiza Viotti, citing ideological motives and an attempt to interfere in Brazil's 2026 presidential election. The move was labeled as false and retaliatory due to Brazil's delay in granting agrément to the U.S. nominee, Daniel Perez, whose appointment was not previously communicated to Itamaraty.

item.title: PL terá chapa puro-sangue para o Senado no RJ
item.description: The PL has selected Carlos Jordy as its Senate candidate and Fernanda Louback as its vice-gubernatorial candidate in Rio de Janeiro, following the withdrawal of Márcio Canella from the União Brasil-PP federation and the alliance's declaration of neutrality. Carlos Portinho will seek Senate re-election after the withdrawal and ineligibility of former governor Cláudio Castro. The move reflects the collapse of the regional coalition and the PL's decision to run a single-party ticket.

item.title: PL homologa André do Prado ao Senado e lança 162 candidatos às eleições proporcionais em SP
item.description: São Paulo's PL party homologated André do Prado, president of the State Legislative Assembly, as its Senate candidate for the 2026 elections, alongside 70 federal and 92 state deputy candidates. The convention did not reference support for the majoritarian ticket, including Governor Tarcísio de Freitas' re-election or Guilherme Derrite's Senate bid, raising questions about state-level alliances. The party has until August 15 to register candidates with the Electoral Justice, allowing for potential changes to the slates.

item.title: PSDB oficializa candidatura de Paula Belmonte ao Palácio do Buriti
item.description: The PSDB officially launched Paula Belmonte's candidacy for Governor of the Federal District during a party convention on Tuesday, August 4. The district deputy emphasized her commitment to transparency, the preservation of the Bank of Brasília (BRB), and strengthening public health, including surgical campaigns. She has not yet chosen a running mate but is in talks with allies, including former senator Antônio Reguffe (União), and aims to finalize the ticket by the 15th.

item.title: Governo Lula chama justificativas dos EUA sobre visto de “falsas”
item.description: The Lula government criticized the U.S. decision to revoke the visa of Brazilian Ambassador Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti, calling the U.S. justifications 'false' and claiming the move is part of an ideologically motivated hostile escalation. It also accused the U.S. of publicly naming its ambassador nominee before submitting a formal agrément request, breaching confidentiality, and denied entry to two U.S. officials who intended to challenge the integrity of Brazil’s electoral system.

item.title: Empresa de amigo de Lulinha tem R$ 182 mi em contratos com RJ, PR e MG
item.description: 3Structure It, a technology company linked to Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha), secured R$ 182 million in contracts with the states of Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, and Minas Gerais between December 2022 and July 2026. The Federal Police is investigating alleged influence peddling by Lulinha to facilitate these contracts, and Minister Flávio Dino has authorized a third inquiry against him. Despite the state governments being oppositional to President Lula, the contracts were signed during their administrations.

item.title: A reação do governo Lula à revogação de visto da embaixadora brasileira nos EUA
item.description: The Lula government condemned the revocation of the Brazilian ambassador’s U.S. visa as part of a deliberate escalation of hostile measures, rejecting U.S. justifications as false. Brasilia argues that the agrément process is confidential under the Vienna Convention and that Washington prematurely disclosed its nominee’s name before formal request. The government also criticized the denial of U.S. officials’ visas, who sought to undermine confidence in Brazil’s electoral system.

item.title: Flávio anuncia vice nesta quarta
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), senator and pre-candidate for the 2026 Brazilian presidency, will announce his running mate on Wednesday, April 5, at 11 a.m., in Brasília. The press conference will formalize the ticket, following hints he gave in a Tuesday interview with O Antagonista and G4. The move underscores his campaign preparations ahead of the 2026 election.

item.title: Lula sanciona lei que cria filtro de relevância para recursos no STJ
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed a law establishing a relevance filter for appeals at the Superior Court of Justice (STJ), aiming to reduce case overload by requiring parties to demonstrate economic, political, social, or legal relevance for appeal admission. The mechanism, already foreseen in Constitutional Amendment No. 125/2022, will allow the STJ to focus on national-impact controversies, with irrevocable decisions and the power to suspend similar cases nationwide for up to one year. Lula stated the measure brings hope for faster justice, while STJ and government officials emphasized that the filter qualifies, rather than denies, access to justice.

item.title: Assessor de Lula diz que recebeu R$ 249 mil de lobista investigada pela PF
item.description: Former chief of staff to Lula, Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro (Marcola), confirmed receiving R$ 249 thousand from lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, who is under investigation by the Federal Police for alleged involvement in the INSS scheme. He stated the amount was a personal loan, already repaid, and that he has made his banking and tax records available to justice, while also hiring a lawyer to prove the transaction.

item.title: Após Republicanos e PP, Podemos também descarta apoio a Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Podemos has decided to remain neutral in the 2026 presidential election and ruled out supporting Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), deepening his isolation following similar rejections from Republicans and PP. The decision, announced by party president Renata Abreu, was made after consultations with state directories and leaders, emphasizing dialogue and concrete solutions to social issues over political polarization. This undermines Bolsonaro’s PL strategy to build a broader coalition before the party conventions close.

item.title: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro concentram críticas de adversários durante sabatina de O Antagonista
item.description: During a series of interviews hosted by O Antagonista and G4, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro were the main targets of criticism from other presidential candidates. The interviews aimed to confront proposals on economic, institutional, and governability issues in a highly polarized electoral context.

item.title: Marcola diz que recebeu R$ 249 mil de lobista do Careca do INSS
item.description: Marcola, former chief of staff to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, stated he received a personal loan of R$ 249,000 from lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, who is under PF investigation for influence peddling. He said the amount was repaid via bank transfer and offered his banking and fiscal secrecy to justice, without disclosing loan terms. The case is linked to suspicions surrounding the 'Careca do INSS' Social Security fraud scheme.

item.title: Governo Lula diz que justificativas usadas pelos EUA são falsas e que há 'interesse descabido' de interferência nas eleições
item.description: The Lula government denounced the revocation of the Brazilian ambassador’s visa in the U.S. as false and part of a deliberate escalation of hostile measures driven by ideological motives, with an improper interest in interfering in Brazil’s 2026 presidential election. The U.S. move was a response to Brazil’s delay in granting agrément to ambassador nominee Daniel Perez, whose name was publicly announced by the U.S. before submitting the formal request, breaching diplomatic confidentiality. Brazil stressed there is no legal deadline for agrément and recalled prior U.S. sanctions on Brazilian officials, including visa cancellations based on unfounded claims of political persecution.

item.title: Vice de Flávio está entre Michelle, Rogério Marinho e Priscila Costa
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) will announce his 2026 presidential running mate by Wednesday, choosing between Senator Rogério Marinho (PL-RN), former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro, and Fortaleza councilwoman Priscila Costa. Campaign coordinator Rogério Marinho said the decision will be made by 10 a.m. Wednesday, with Centrão leaders favoring him due to his expressed desire to be vice.

item.title: Governo Lula 'repudia' retirada de visto de embaixadora e diz que justificativas dos EUA 'são falsas'
item.description: The Lula government repudiated the U.S. decision to revoke the visa of Brazil's ambassador to Washington, calling the American justifications false and a violation of international law, particularly the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations. Brazil argues the U.S. publicly announced its ambassador nominee before submitting the formal agrément request, which is improper, and that the process remains under review. The Brazilian government views this as part of a deliberate escalation of hostile measures driven by ideological motives and aimed at interfering in the 2026 presidential election.

item.title: Ex-chefe de gabinete de Lula diz que devolveu R$ 249 mil a empresária amiga de Lulinha
item.description: Former chief of staff to President Lula, Marco Aurélio Marcola, stated he repaid a personal loan of R$ 249,000 obtained from businesswoman Roberta Luchsinger via bank transfer, making his banking and fiscal secrets available to justice to prove the transaction was strictly private. The payment emerged amid PF investigations into alleged influence-peddling involving Lula’s eldest son, Fábio Luís (Lulinha), and negotiations in the medicinal cannabis market, in which Luchsinger is also under scrutiny.

item.title: Lobista pagou R$ 249 mil em contas pessoais de Marcola, ex-chefe de gabinete de Lula
item.description: Former Chief of Staff to President Lula, Marco Aurélio Santana (Marcola), received R$ 249,000 from lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger to pay personal expenses in 2025, according to a Federal Police investigation. The payments, made via barcode slips to avoid a paper trail, are part of a third inquiry probing whether Marcola engaged in influence peddling using his government position. The case, overseen by Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino, also examines ties to Lula’s son, Lulinha, who allegedly benefited from Roberta’s payments for a luxury trip to Finland and a Brasília mansion rental.

item.title: Candidatos à presidência se posicionam sobre o STF, anistia e reformas do Judiciário
item.description: In a O Antagonista forum, 2026 presidential candidates discussed the Supreme Federal Court's (STF) role, potential amnesty for January 8th participants, and 12 proposed judicial reforms, revealing sharp divides between those defending judicial independence and critics accusing the Court of overreof judicial supremacy. Proposals such as creating a Supreme Court oversight council and revising the general repercussion mechanism were central to the discussion, highlighting tensions over checks and balances in Brazil’s democracy.

item.title: Ex-chefe de gabinete de Lula diz que pagou R$ 249 mil para quitar empréstimo com amiga de Lulinha
item.description: Former chief of staff to President Lula, Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro (Marcola), said he paid R$249,000 to settle a personal loan with lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, who is under PF investigation for suspected influence peddling with Lulinha. He stated the transaction was private, made his banking and tax secrecy available to justice, hired a lawyer, and emphasized Lula’s continued trust in him.

item.title: Quem é Gabriela Hardt, juíza afastada do cargo por dois anos por atos na Operação Lava Jato
item.description: The National Council of Justice (CNJ) removed Judge Gabriela Hardt from office for two years over actions taken during her tenure in Operation Car Wash, including the annulled conviction of Lula in the Atibaia case and plagiarism allegations regarding Sergio Moro’s rulings. Hardt temporarily presided over the 13th Federal Court in Curitiba during Moro’s absences and later his resignation to join Bolsonaro’s government, issuing controversial rulings such as the temporary detention of José Dirceu and the partial release of Lula’s blocked assets. A Paraná native, she became a federal judge in 2009 after graduating from UFPR, where Moro once taught.

item.title: Podemos anuncia neutralidade na disputa presidencial de 2026
item.description: Podemos announced neutrality in the 2026 presidential race after nationwide consultations with state directories, leaders, and members. The decision, made by national president Renata Abreu, aims to counter political polarization and focus on concrete solutions to issues like violence, bureaucracy, and access to services. Parties such as Republicans, Brazil Union, and PP also chose neutrality, ruling out support for Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Renata Abreu oficializa neutralidade do Podemos na disputa à Presidência
item.description: Podemos officially declared neutrality in the 2026 presidential race, following other parties such as União Brasil, PP, and Republicanos, which also chose not to endorse any presidential candidate. The decision came after extensive consultations with state directories, leaders, and members nationwide, with party president Renata Abreu stating the party prioritizes solving real-world problems—like supporting atypical mothers, victims of violence, and entrepreneurs—over ideological polarization. This stance rules out the possibility of Abreu serving as Flávio Bolsonaro’s running mate, as his campaign now prepares to announce a vice-presidential pick on Wednesday, the 5th.

item.title: Lindbergh sobre ação dos EUA: "Flávio e Eduardo devem estar em festa"
item.description: Federal deputy Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ) criticized the Trump administration's revocation of the visa of Brazil's ambassador to the U.S., Maria Luiza Viotti, calling it unacceptable and an interference in Brazilian diplomacy. He linked the move to Flávio and Eduardo Bolsonaro's alignment with U.S. far-right factions, suggesting they were celebrating the crisis, and urged President Lula to maintain a firm stance against external pressures.

item.title: Após 40 anos de mandatos, Aécio desiste de disputar eleição em 2026
item.description: Deputy Aécio Neves (PSDB-MG) announced he will not run for any elective office in 2026 after 40 consecutive years in office. He cited the polarization between Lula and Bolsonaro as a reason for abandoning presidential and Senate bids, despite leading polls in Minas Gerais. Aécio said he will remain at the helm of the PSDB to lead a new national project that is liberal, inclusive, and pragmatic.

item.title: Maioria do Congresso vê benefício eleitoral para Lula com escala 6 X 1
item.description: Most of Congress believes that reducing the workweek to 40 hours (ending the 6x1 scale) will electorally benefit President Lula in 2026, with 72.8% of deputies and 67.9% of senators seeing a positive or very positive impact. The Ranking dos Políticos survey shows the issue is already shaping the political landscape, even before final approval, as lawmakers avoid public opposition to avoid hurting Lula’s electoral prospects.

item.title: Greve dos ferroviários é mantida em SP e seguirá na quarta-feira (5)
item.description: Railway workers on CPTM Lines 11, 12 and 13 have maintained their strike over alleged lack of written job security guarantees following the concession to Trivia Trens. The São Paulo government under Tarcísio de Freitas claims job preservation was assured and provides workforce redistribution data, which the union disputes. The strike has caused major disruptions in the eastern zone of São Paulo and surrounding cities, prompting contingency measures including early metro openings and bus substitutions.

item.title: Saída de Girão acaba com racha no CE que gerou a briga de Michelle e Flávio
item.description: The announcement that Senator Eduardo Girão (Novo-CE) will be the vice-presidential candidate on the ticket led by former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo-MG) ends the major rift in Bolsonarism generated in Ceará, where Girão was a pre-candidate for state governor. His decision to withdraw from the gubernatorial race to join the national ticket unifies Bolsonarist forces in the state.

item.title: Lula faz aceno duplo a caminhoneiros e motoristas de aplicativo
item.description: President Lula will sign PLV nº 6/2026, which regulates transport operations, CIOT generation, and compliance with the National Minimum Freight Floor Policy, in a ceremony at 4 p.m. at the Planalto Palace. Later, at 5 p.m., he will meet with app-based drivers and taxi drivers to discuss the Move program, which offers reduced-interest loans for new or used vehicles, alongside Minister Guilherme Boulos.

item.title: Tenente Dalma é oficializada pelo PRTB como candidata à vice-presidência da República na chapa de Leonardo Avalanche
item.description: The Brazilian Labor Renewal Party (PRTB) officially nominated Lieutenant Dalma Regina Florencio de Morais as its vice-presidential candidate on the ticket with Leonardo Avalanche. The decision was unanimously approved by the party's National Executive Committee on August 3. Avalanche's presidential candidacy had been announced at a party convention on July 29, where he advocated for a single tax reform to reduce taxation and stimulate economic growth.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro deve anunciar vice nesta quarta
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a pre-candidate for President of Brazil, is expected to announce his running mate for vice president this Wednesday (5). He had previously set August 15 as the deadline for finalizing the ticket, the last day to register candidacies with the Electoral Justice. The announcement comes during his remote participation in a sabatina hosted by 'O Antagonista' and G4.

item.title: Governo Tarcísio diz que greve de ferroviários é baseada em "desinformação"
item.description: The government of Tarcísio de Freitas claims the railway workers' strike on CPTM lines 11-Coral, 12-Safira and 13-Jade is based on misinformation and harms nearly 1 million passengers, while contributing to over 720 km of traffic congestion in São Paulo. Workers defend the strike's legality under the Constitution, reject being labeled 'vagabonds,' and say they are fighting for their jobs and against privatizations. The government activated a contingency plan to reduce the strike's impacts.

item.title: Eleições 2026: TSE recebe lista de gestores públicos com contas julgadas irregulares
item.description: The TSE received from the TCU a list of over 6,1 thousand public officials with accounts judged irregular in the last eight years, 3% fewer than in 2024. Most cases involve former mayors and councilors from small towns, concentrated in the Northeast and Southeast regions. Of the 266 politically exposed individuals, there are 135 councilors, 1 councilors, 114 mayors, six state deputies, two federal deputies, and one senator (including alternates).

item.title: Embaixadora brasileira poderá ficar em Washington, dizem EUA
item.description: The U.S. State Department revoked the visa of Brazilian Ambassador Maria Luiza Viotti in Washington as a reciprocal measure due to Brazil's delay in granting agrément to Donald Trump's nominee for U.S. ambassador to Brasília. The department clarified it is not a persona non grata declaration but warned that if the ambassador leaves the U.S., she would need a new visa to return.

item.title: “Os únicos com coragem de combater os intocáveis”, diz Zema sobre Girão
item.description: Romeu Zema praised the official nomination of Eduardo Girão as his vice-presidential running mate, stating they are the only ones with courage to confront the 'to the elite', referring to Supreme Court justices. Zema commended Girão’s integrity, faith, and entrepreneurial success. The Novo ticket positions itself as a direct challenge to Brazil’s judiciary.

item.title: Lobista de Careca do INSS celebrou ida de Flávio Dino ao STF
item.description: Roberta Luchsinger, a lobbyist under investigation for possible influence peddling on behalf of Antônio Carlos Camilo Antunes (Careca do INSS), celebrated Flávio Dino’s nomination to the STF in November 2023, praising him as honest, brave, and northeastern. She is a friend of Lulinha (Fábio Luís Lula da Silva) and is investigated for making payments of tens of thousands of reais to Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro (Marcola), former chief of staff to President Lula, who claims the transfers were a personal loan. Dino, appointed by Lula to replace Rosa Weber on the STF, currently oversees one of the investigations into Lulinha.

item.title: Sem precedentes, diz Ricupero após EUA revogar visto de embaixadora
item.description: Former minister Rubens Ricupero stated that the U.S. revocation of Brazil’s ambassador’s visa is an unprecedented act, likely retaliation for Brazil’s refusal to accept Daniel Perez as the U.S. nominee. He linked the move to broader diplomatic tensions, including the denial of visas to U.S. officials seeking to meet with presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, and warned that without resolution, both embassies could be led by chargés d’affaires.

item.title: Operação mira grupo suspeito de planejar ataque a Palácio do Planalto em outubro
item.description: Eight people were targeted in a search and seizure operation on suspicion of planning attacks against the Planalto Palace and other buildings on the Ministries Esplanade in October, during the 2026 electoral period. The police action aims to investigate potential threats to democratic institutions amid a sensitive phase of the electoral calendar.

item.title: TRE rejeita ação de aliados de Elmano de Freitas e valida apoio de federação União-Progressista a Ciro Gomes no CE
item.description: The Ceará Regional Electoral Court (TRE-CE) rejected a lawsuit by allies of Governor Elmano de Freitas (PT) seeking to invalidate the União-Progressista federation’s support for Ciro Gomes (PSDB) in the state. By a 4–2 vote, the court ruled that federated parties cannot act independently of the federation, upholding the official endorsement of Ciro Gomes, with Roberto Cláudio as vice-presidential candidate and Capitão Wagner as Senate nominee.

item.title: Podemos decide por neutralidade nas eleições presidenciais
item.description: The Podemos party announced neutrality in the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections, joining other parties such as União Brasil, Progressistas (PP), and Republicans. The decision, communicated by party president Renata Abreu, aims to promote dialogue and concrete solutions amid political polarization. This stance disrupted negotiations with Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL-RJ) campaign, which had been seeking Podemos’ support for a vice-presidential candidate but remains undecided as the registration deadline approaches.

item.title: MJ detalha operação para desarticular ataques a Brasília
item.description: The Ministry of Justice and Public Security detailed Operation Rede Interrompida, which dismantled a suspected group planning attacks in Brasília during the October electoral period, including invasions of public buildings and a bomb attack during electoral debates. The investigation began in June following Ciberlab monitoring of Telegram groups and involved police forces from five states, resulting in eight search and seizure warrants.

item.title: Lula evita ir à convenção de Leandro Grass para não desagradar PSB
item.description: Lula avoids attending Leandro Grass's (PT) convention in the Federal District to avoid displeasing the PSB, whose candidate, Cappelli, he appointed as federal intervener after the January 8 attacks. The move highlights tensions among Lula's allies in the local race, where PT and PSB, despite being national allies, field competing candidates. The Brazil of Hope Federation postponed its convention to August 5 to broaden the democratic and popular front supporting Grass.

item.title: Senado sedia exposição 'O Caminho do Voto', sobre etapas do processo eleitoral
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre attended the opening of the exhibition 'O Caminho do Voto', organized by the TSE, which illustrates the stages of Brazil's electoral process, from electronic voting machine development and testing to vote casting and result tabulation. The exhibition, hosted at the Espaço Senador Ivandro Cunha Lima, will be open until August 21, initially in the Senate and later moving to the Espaço da Praça das Abelhas, as part of National Electronic Voting System Week. The exhibit emphasizes the security and integrity of Brazil's electoral system, regarded as one of the most secure in the world.

item.title: Vera Lúcia é registrada pelo PSTU como candidata a governadora de SP e declara não ter bens
item.description: The PSTU has registered Vera Lúcia as its candidate for governor of São Paulo, with Renata França as her running mate. The sociologist declared before the TSE that she owns no assets, a shift from previous elections where she reported small holdings, such as R$8,800 in savings in 2022 and a R$20,000 land plot in 2020. This marks her fourth attempt to win an executive office in general elections, having previously run for president in 2018 and 2022, for governor of Sergipe in 2010, and for federal deputy in 2006 and 2014 — all without success.

item.title: Múcio diz que solução para invasão dos EUA seria ‘abrir o portão’
item.description: Defense Minister José Múcio stated that in the event of a hypothetical U.S. military invasion, Brazil should 'open the gate' due to lacking equipment and financial resources to resist, emphasizing that the current 1% of GDP allocated to defense is inadequate for long-term deterrence and technological development. His remarks contrast with President Lula’s recent rhetoric of national strength and sovereignty amid U.S.-Brazil diplomatic tensions, including the U.S. designation of PCC and CV as terrorist organizations and Trump’s threats to seize Greenland, Canada, and the Panama Canal.

item.title: Mendonça nega remover vídeo de Flávio que associa PT ao PCC
item.description: TSE Minister André Mendonça denied a preliminary injunction request by the Brazil of Hope Federation (PT, PCdoB, and PV) to take down a video posted by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) linking the PT to criminal factions PCC and CV. The ruling keeps the video online despite claims it defames the party and incites political hatred.

item.title: Aécio Neves desiste de disputar eleição pela primeira vez em 40 anos
item.description: Aécio Neves announced he will not run for any office in the 2026 elections, ending a 40-year streak of consecutive candidacies. Although well-positioned for the Senate in Minas Gerais, he chose to focus on leading the PSDB nationally and building a centrist political project, seeking to move beyond Lula-Bolsonaro polarization.
